text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Eurotunnel banks to control 45.5 percent of the Channel tunnel operator's capital, at a price of 10.40 francs a share, existing shareholders holding 54 percent under a debt-restructuring agreement presented yesterday. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Savings banks Caisses d'Epargne will not bid for controlling stake in CIC, leaving BNP and Societe Generale in the race.
-- Elf Aquitaine sells 2.9 percent stake in Compagnie de Suez, to Belgian group owned by businessman Albert Frere.
-- BNP and Dresdner Bank sign co-operation agreement.
-- Call money under 3.5 percent is currently at lowest level in 25 years, Bank of France may further cut intervention rate.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe to open wage negotiations with civil servants in 1997.

-- Some 20 percent of France Telecom to be offered for sale to the public in April 1997, says telecommunications minister Francois Fillon. He hopes a third major telephone operator will emerge to compete with France Telecom and Cegetel, a joint venture between Generale des Eaux, British Telecom, SBC Communications Inc and Mannesmann AG.
-- Tendering deadline for bankrupt airline Air Liberte is October 14, British Airways and AOM interested.

-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says buying Thomson-CSF would allow shared financing of research and development, build group able to compete with U.S. leader firms, adds Alcatel would need no outside financial help to acquire Thomson.
-- Use of law on part-time work may help reduce by one third the number of planned job cuts at Moulinex appliance manufacturer's plants.
-- Leclerc supermarkets chain launches campaign allowing customers to familiarise with future European single currency euro in real-life situations.
